response.sql: SELECT AVG("rebrate" / "feerate") AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM "fees" WHERE "feerate" > 0.0009;

assumptions.assumption: Missing values are NULLs in rebrate. AVG skips rows where rebrate is NULL, and the WHERE clause excludes NULL feerate. Because feerate > 0.0009, the division never hits zero.
"How many such fee records" means every fee row with feerate > 0.0009, including rows whose rebrate is NULL. If it means only rows that contribute to the average, the count should use COUNT(rebrate).

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the fee records that have a usable ratio, meaning rebrate is also non-NULL, so the count matches the rows that feed the average.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG("rebrate" / "feerate") AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT("rebrate") AS fee_record_count FROM "fees" WHERE "feerate" > 0.0009;
